learning_outcomes.text: Obtain a prediction model based on the simple linear regression model.
Perform a critical analysis of the assumptions on which the model is based, and statistically analyze whether these are verified using statistical inference techniques.
Adequately apply multiple linear regression techniques and perform an inferential statistical analysis of the model's assumptions.
Know the different types of time series and the components of a time series.
Apply exponential smoothing models to make predictions with a time series.
Use ARIMA models, adequately estimating their components and making predictions.
Critically analyze the models and apply the most appropriate one in each case.
Apply predictive modeling techniques to real data cases.

syllabus_topics: Predictive models according to data type. Basic steps in prediction. Statistics in predictive models.
Simple linear regression. Model formulation and estimation. Model assumptions. Inference for model parameters. Goodness of fit. Prediction.

Multiple linear regression. Model formulation and estimation. Model assumptions. Inference for model parameters. ANOVA and model fitting. Model selection. Use of qualitative predictors. Model diagnostics and multicollinearity.
Predictions for time-measured data. Decomposition of time series: location, trend, and seasonality. Simple prediction methods. Linear models in time series. Goodness of fit. Model validation.
Exponential smoothing models: basic, double, triple. Likelihood-based models.
Stationarity. Lag operators. Autoregressive models. Moving average models. Non-seasonal and seasonal ARIMA models.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum score of 3.5 out of 10 in the final theoretical-practical exam (F) is mandatory to pass. If the minimum in F is not reached, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. In extraordinary calls, students can either maintain their continuous assessment scores or retake theoretical and practical continuous assessment tests. For all cases, a minimum score in the main exam (F, FT) of at least 3.5 out of 10 is required; otherwise, the final grade is capped at 4.0. For the early extraordinary call and differentiated evaluation, the final grade is calculated as 0.60FT + 0.40FP, with a minimum of 3.5 out of 10 required in the theoretical exam (FT), otherwise the grade is capped at 4.0.
